summary.intent: Execute Phase 35 (Phala Testnet TEE Migration) — restructure the TEE worker into the monorepo, integrate Phala SDK, add tests/observability, update CI/CD, deploy a live CVM to Phala Cloud, and verify end-to-end IPNS republish.
summary.outcome: All 6 plans completed across 4 waves, CVM deployed and live on Phala Cloud production infrastructure, epoch key determinism and IPNS republish verified, phase marked complete with a follow-up security review and code cleanup committed.

repo: The phase was named 'phala-testnet-tee-migration' but Phala Cloud has no separate testnet — the free tier ($20 credit) runs on the same production nodes (Intel TDX hardware, dstack-pha-prod5) as paid deployments.

The TEE worker was relocated from root `tee-worker/` to `apps/tee-worker/` and now delegates to shared monorepo packages: `@cipherbox/core` for IPNS signing, `@cipherbox/crypto` for ECIES, `@cipherbox/sdk-core` for KuboProvider/PsaProvider.
The `public-key.ts` route was calling `getKeypair()` instead of `getPublicKey()`, leaking the private key into route scope — caught and fixed during /simplify.
Health route used `TEE_EPOCH` env var while the migrate route used `TEE_CURRENT_EPOCH` — inconsistent and was reading the wrong variable.
The `/republish` endpoint had no batch size limit, allowing unbounded ECIES decryption as a DoS vector — fixed with MAX_BATCH_SIZE=100.
Prometheus metrics middleware used `req.path` as a label for unmatched routes, creating unbounded label cardinality — fixed by normalizing to `'unmatched'`.
The Docker host for the project is at `192.168.133.12` (was previously documented as `192.168.133.114`).
TEE worker image pushed to GHCR as `ghcr.io/fsm1/cipherbox-tee-worker:v35-amd64`.

code.finding: Called `getKeypair()` instead of `getPublicKey()` — was exposing private key in route scope. Fixed to use `getPublicKey()`.
Used `TEE_EPOCH` env var but the correct var is `TEE_CURRENT_EPOCH` (consistent with migrate route).

No batch size limit — added MAX_BATCH_SIZE=100 guard. Also removed dead `keyEpoch` field from response interface and replaced redundant mutable `successes`/`failures` counters with derived values from results array.
Used `req.path` as a Prometheus label value for 404/unmatched routes — unbounded cardinality. Fixed to use the string `'unmatched'` as fallback.

workflow: GSD worktree-based parallel execution can produce git config lock contention when two agents run simultaneously on the same repo — running Wave 2 agents sequentially instead of in parallel resolved the issue.

The GSD `pause-work` / `resume-work` handoff workflow successfully preserved full session state (credentials, task position, blocker context) across a machine transfer from dev machine to Docker host.
The `classifyHandoffIfNeeded` Claude Code runtime bug can fire after a successful agent execution — spot-check via SUMMARY.md existence and git log rather than trusting the error signal.
After a worktree merge, STATE.md and ROADMAP.md frequently produce merge conflicts; resolving by taking the agent's version is correct since the agent updated these files last.
Phala CLI (`phala`) v1.1.13 is installable via npm and supports `deploy`, `restart`, and health-check operations against Phala Cloud CVMs.
The `@cipherbox/crypto` package must be built (`pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build`) before it can be imported in ad-hoc Node scripts for testing.

friction: Wave 2 parallel agents failed: one hit a git config lock (concurrent worktree creation), the other was interrupted by a usage limit mid-execution — required sequential retry.
Usage limit hit mid-session required a user 'continue' prompt before work could resume.
`gsd-tools init execute-phase` returned `phase_found: false` when run from the main repo because the active work was in a worktree — required detecting the worktree path and re-running from there.
The session transfer to the Docker host required multiple `git fetch && git pull` attempts before the pushed branch was visible.
The handoff HANDOFF.json noted an uncommitted Dockerfile change that was actually already committed by the Docker host session — stale data in handoff.
The `phala restart` command caused ~90+ seconds of downtime with several failed health checks before the CVM came back up, requiring multiple retry loops.
Phase name 'phala-testnet-tee-migration' is a permanent misnomer since there is no Phala testnet — cannot rename without breaking cross-references in planning artifacts.
open_items: Probe/connection-test deduplication: `connection-test.ts` in tee-worker duplicates probe logic from `@cipherbox/sdk-core` — deferred as significant refactor.
Sequential batch processing in `/republish` is a deliberate security tradeoff (no concurrent ECIES decryption) but could be revisited for performance if needed.
String zeroing via `.fill(0)` after ECIES operations is a best-effort measure — JavaScript GC makes true memory clearing impossible; a comment exists but this is a fundamental language limitation.
Security review report generated at `.planning/security/REVIEW-phase-35.md` — findings should be triaged and addressed in a follow-up phase or gap closure.
The `PHALA_CLOUD_API_KEY` in the handoff/transcript is now committed to planning docs (HANDOFF.json) — should verify it has been rotated or is acceptable to expose in the repo.
Phase 35 branch `phase-35-phala-testnet-tee-migration` needs to be merged to main via PR — `/gsd:ship` was suggested but not executed.
